testName: Class A Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: Which vehicle requires a CDL license?

options.text: A military vehicle
A school bus
An emergency vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: A school bus
questions.explanation: A CDL is not required for military vehicles, emergency vehicles, farm equipment, or recreational vehicles. A CDL is also not required for a straight truck with only your personal property. However, a CDL is required for a school bus.

questions.question: When checking air and electrical lines during a vehicle inspection, which should NOT be true?

options.text: The air hoses are making a hissing noise.
The air hoses and electrical lines are not cut.
The air lines are not pinched.
The air lines are not dragging against tractor parts.

questions.correctAnswerText: The air hoses are making a hissing noise.
questions.explanation: Check air and electrical lines for leaks. Make sure they are not cut, worn, or chafed. Check that they are not tangled, pinched, or dragging against tractor parts.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should NOT:

options.text: Decrease your speed.
Increase your speed.
Use your low beam headlights.
Turn on your four-way flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your speed.
questions.explanation: When driving through fog, slow down. Use your low beam headlights and fog lights. Turn on your four-way flashers.

questions.question: Why should you do routine vehicle inspections?

options.text: Safety.
Good gas mileage.
Comfort.

questions.correctAnswerText: Safety.
questions.explanation: Inspecting your vehicle helps keep you and other road users safe.

questions.question: In very hot weather, why should you check your tires regularly?

options.text: They may melt.
Air pressure may increase with the temperature.
The tread wears down extra quickly.
The lug nuts may loosen.

questions.correctAnswerText: Air pressure may increase with the temperature.
questions.explanation: Heat causes air to expand. In very hot weather, tire air pressure can get too high. If this happens, stop and let your tires cool. Do not let air out, as the pressure will drop too low when the tires cool down.

questions.question: During backing exercises (not straight line), you can exit your vehicle to check its position no more than:

options.text: One time.
Two times.
Three times.
Four times.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two times.
questions.explanation: You can exit your vehicle to check its position during a basic control skills test. During straight line backing, you can only do this once. During other exercises, you can do this up to two times.

questions.question: Which crime would NOT disqualify someone from getting a hazmat endorsement?

options.text: Arson
Dishonesty
Robbery
Littering

questions.correctAnswerText: Littering
questions.explanation: Crimes that disqualify someone for seven years include arson, robbery, and dishonesty or fraud. More serious crimes like murder result in a lifetime ban.

questions.question: A vehicle stopped at a green light may mean the driver:

options.text: Is impaired.
Is colorblind.
Does not know the rules of the road.
Is very patient.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is impaired.
questions.explanation: Watch for signs that a driver may be impaired by alcohol, drugs, sleep deprivation, or illness. One sign is stopping at inappropriate places, like green traffic lights.

questions.question: When backing a truck, you should:

options.text: Only use the side mirrors on the driver's side.
Use both side mirrors.
Not use a helper.
Only use the mirror on the passenger's side.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both side mirrors.
questions.explanation: Check both side mirrors frequently when backing. Use a helper to watch your blind spots whenever possible.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection skills test, you must:

options.text: Explain to the examiner what should be checked and why.
Let the examiner check the vehicle.
Talk to a mechanic to prove your knowledge.
Take apart the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Explain to the examiner what should be checked and why.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection skills test, explain to the examiner what you are checking and why.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a sign of fatigue?

options.text: Trouble focusing and blinking a lot
Yawning often or rubbing your eyes
Staying in your lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Staying in your lane
questions.explanation: Signs of fatigue include trouble focusing, frequent blinking, heavy eyelids, yawning, rubbing your eyes, daydreaming, wandering thoughts, not remembering the last few miles, missing exits or signs, trouble holding your head up, drifting from your lane, following too closely, hitting a shoulder rumble strip, and feeling restless or irritable.

questions.question: When checking power steering fluid during a vehicle inspection, you do NOT need to:

options.text: Show where the power steering fluid dipstick is located
Check that there is enough power steering fluid
Make sure the power steering fluid level is above the full mark
Make sure the power steering fluid level is above the refill mark

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the power steering fluid level is above the full mark
questions.explanation: During a vehicle inspection, you must locate the power steering fluid dipstick and check that there is enough fluid. The fluid level must be above the refill mark, not the full mark.

questions.question: When traveling with cargo, you must check that it is secure:

options.text: No more than two times
Every 150 miles or three hours of driving
Only after going up a hill
Only after a hard stop

questions.correctAnswerText: Every 150 miles or three hours of driving
questions.explanation: Check your cargo before you start, within the first 50 miles, and then every three hours or 150 miles of driving. The driver is responsible for keeping the cargo safe and secure the entire trip.

questions.question: If another vehicle is tailgating you, you should:

options.text: Speed up
Increase the space between your vehicle and the one ahead of you
Make quick movements

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the space between your vehicle and the one ahead of you
questions.explanation: If you are being tailgated, increase the distance between your vehicle and the vehicle ahead. This gives you more room to change speed or direction, and makes it easier for the tailgater to pass.

questions.question: Before entering a curve, you should:

options.text: Upshift
Speed up
Drive on the shoulder
Downshift

questions.correctAnswerText: Downshift
questions.explanation: Always downshift before a curve. Slowing down before you enter the curve helps you keep better control of your vehicle.

questions.question: If an air compressor has a belt drive, the belt should be checked to make sure it is:

options.text: Thin
Properly tightened
Cracked

questions.correctAnswerText: Properly tightened
questions.explanation: If your vehicle has air brakes with a belt-driven compressor, check the belt before each trip. Make sure the belt is tight and in good condition.

questions.question: A load that is 10 feet long must be secured with at least:

options.text: One tie-down
Two tie-downs
Three tie-downs

questions.correctAnswerText: Two tie-downs
questions.explanation: Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. However, all cargo must have at least two tie-downs, no matter the size.

questions.question: When driving, you should:

options.text: Always drive at the posted speed limit
Always drive slightly below the posted speed limit
Adjust your speed based on road and traffic conditions
Drive as fast as possible

questions.correctAnswerText: Adjust your speed based on road and traffic conditions
questions.explanation: Driving too fast causes many fatal crashes. You must constantly adjust your speed to match the road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, if one system loses air pressure:

options.text: All brakes will stop working
Either the front or rear brakes will not work fully
There is usually no noticeable effect

questions.correctAnswerText: Either the front or rear brakes will not work fully
questions.explanation: In a dual air brake system, either the front or rear brakes will not work fully if one system loses pressure. If the air pressure gets too low while driving, exit the road and park as soon as you can.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection of power steering hoses, you should look for:

options.text: Leaks
Secure connections to the battery
Extra hose pieces available for repairs

questions.correctAnswerText: Leaks
questions.explanation: When inspecting a vehicle with power steering, check the hoses, pumps, and fluid level. Look closely at the hoses for any leaks.

questions.question: During the on-road driving test, you should:

options.text: Create your own route to show your driving skills.
Follow the examiner's directions.
Bring a passenger to ride with you.
Drive in an unsafe way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the examiner's directions.
questions.explanation: During the on-road driving test, follow the directions the examiner gives you. The examiner will never ask you to drive unsafely.

questions.question: Federal and state laws require:

options.text: Drivers to regularly inspect their vehicles.
Drivers to inspect vehicles only if they think there may be a problem.
Drivers to inspect vehicles only before traveling out-of-state.
Drivers to inspect vehicles only when transporting hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers to regularly inspect their vehicles.
questions.explanation: Commercial drivers must inspect their vehicles before every trip by federal and state law. Regular inspections help drivers find problems before they become dangerous or expensive.

questions.question: During the pre-trip vehicle inspection test:

options.text: You do not need to identify the ABS.
Windshield wipers do not need to be checked.
Shock absorbers only need to be checked on one axle.
Check the steering box for leaks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the steering box for leaks.
questions.explanation: During the external inspection part of the pre-trip vehicle inspection test, you must check that the steering box is securely mounted and has no leaks.

questions.question: To prevent your tires and engine from overheating in very hot weather, you should:

options.text: Drive faster.
Drive slower.
Drive on the shoulder.
Drive with your windows down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slower.
questions.explanation: Faster driving makes your engine and tires hotter. In very hot weather, driving slower helps prevent overheating.

questions.question: You must be at least ____ to get a hazardous materials endorsement.

options.text: 15 years old
18 years old
21 years old
25 years old

questions.correctAnswerText: 21 years old
questions.explanation: You must be at least 21 years old and have at least one year of driving experience to drive in interstate commerce or transport hazardous materials.

questions.question: After a crash, you should do all of the following except:

options.text: Protect the area.
Notify the proper authorities.
Care for anyone injured.
Drive away without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive away without stopping.
questions.explanation: After a crash, you must protect the area, notify the authorities, and care for anyone injured. Protecting the accident site helps prevent another crash in the same location.

questions.question: What is a tire load?

options.text: The minimum safe weight a tire can carry
The maximum safe weight a tire can carry
The weight of the tire itself

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe weight a tire can carry
questions.explanation: Tire load is the maximum safe weight a tire can carry at a specific pressure.

questions.question: When backing up with a trailer, you should:

options.text: Do nothing. The vehicle will naturally follow the trailer.
Change the direction of the steering wheel.
Turn the steering wheel harder in the same direction it is already turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change the direction of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: When backing with a trailer, first turn the steering wheel in the opposite direction of the turn you want. Once the trailer starts to turn, reverse the steering wheel direction to follow the trailer.

questions.question: When placing warning triangles on the road, you should:

options.text: Hold the triangles between your body and oncoming traffic.
Carry the triangles behind your back so other drivers do not see them until they are placed.
Hold the triangles as low as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the triangles between your body and oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: For your safety, hold the warning triangles between your body and oncoming traffic when placing them.

questions.question: Always drive so your vehicle can stop:

options.text: Within 10 feet of your current position.
Within 1,000 feet of your current position.
Within the area you can see ahead on the road.
Immediately.

questions.correctAnswerText: Within the area you can see ahead on the road.
questions.explanation: Always drive so you can stop your vehicle within the part of the road you can see ahead of you.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing during the driving test, you should:

options.text: Pass another vehicle on the tracks if it is going too slow.
Get out of your vehicle to check for a train.
Not shift gears while on the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not shift gears while on the tracks.
questions.explanation: During the driving test, do not stop, shift gears, pass other vehicles, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is on railroad tracks.

questions.question: If a vehicle has an inspection report, the driver should:

options.text: Ignore the report and look for problems themselves.
Take the vehicle to a mechanic.
Read the report.
Skip the pre-trip inspection and only use the report.

questions.correctAnswerText: Read the report.
questions.explanation: Start your vehicle inspection by reading the last inspection report. The company should have fixed any problems listed on the report.

questions.question: When turning left with two left turn lanes available, which lane should you use?

options.text: The left lane
The right lane
Either lane
Large trucks should not turn at intersections with two left turn lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane
questions.explanation: Large vehicles need more space to turn left. When two left turn lanes are available, use the right lane to start your turn.

questions.question: What type of brakes do most newer heavy-duty trucks use?

options.text: Single air brakes
Dual air brakes
Triple air brakes

questions.correctAnswerText: Dual air brakes
questions.explanation: Most newer heavy-duty trucks use dual air brake systems. This system has two separate air brakes that work with a single set of brake controls.

questions.question: Convex mirrors:

options.text: Cannot be used on vehicles carrying hazardous materials.
Can replace flat mirrors.
Help you see a wider area.
Are illegal in most states.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you see a wider area.
questions.explanation: Many large vehicles have curved, convex mirrors. These mirrors let you see a wider area than flat mirrors. However, objects appear smaller and farther away than they actually are.

questions.question: When entering an expressway during the skills test, you should:

options.text: Check for traffic.
Not use signals.
Suddenly enter a lane of traffic.
Cut off other drivers if necessary.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for traffic.
questions.explanation: During the driving skills test, you may need to enter an expressway. Always check traffic first, use your signals, and merge smoothly into the proper lane.

questions.question: Regrooved tires are:

options.text: Allowed only on the front of a bus.
Allowed only on the rear of a bus.
Not allowed anywhere on a bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allowed only on the rear of a bus.
questions.explanation: Regrooved, recapped, or retreaded tires cannot be used on the front of a bus.

questions.question: Cargo in a trailer:

options.text: Does not need to be secured.
Should be stacked no higher than three feet.
Should be secured to prevent movement.
Should have heavy items on top of lighter items.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be secured to prevent movement.
questions.explanation: Cargo must be secured to keep it from moving while traveling. Arrange cargo to keep the vehicle's weight centered and balanced.

questions.question: After an accident, use flares with caution because:

options.text: Spilled fuel on the ground could catch fire.
Other drivers may not see flares in sunny weather.
Flares are expensive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spilled fuel on the ground could catch fire.
questions.explanation: Improperly used flares near spilled fuel often cause vehicle fires after accidents. Always use flares with caution.

questions.question: An air compressor governor stops pumping air when the air tanks reach:

options.text: 125 psi
100 psi
150 psi
80 psi

questions.correctAnswerText: 125 psi
questions.explanation: An air compressor governor stops pumping air when the tanks reach 125 psi. This pressure level is called the "cut-out" level.

questions.question: In cold temperatures, bridges usually freeze:

options.text: After other parts of the road.
Before other parts of the road.
At the same time as other parts of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before other parts of the road.
questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before other road surfaces in cold weather. When driving in winter, especially on wet roads, drive slowly and carefully on bridges and overpasses.

questions.question: Placards must be used:

options.text: Any time a vehicle carries hazardous materials.
If there is empty space in the truck.
If hazardous materials weigh more than 200 pounds.
If the hazardous materials create a breathing hazard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any time a vehicle carries hazardous materials.
questions.explanation: Placards must be placed on vehicles that carry hazardous materials. They show what type of material is being carried and warn other drivers of the hazard.

questions.question: When loading a trailer, you should:

options.text: Put as little weight as possible over the axles.
Put the right amount of weight over the axles.
Not worry about how cargo weight is spread out.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put the right amount of weight over the axles.
questions.explanation: The weight on each axle must be balanced. Too much or too little weight can make steering hard, reduce tire grip, or damage the axles.

questions.question: One way to prevent hydroplaning on wet roads is to:

options.text: Keep your tires with good tread depth.
Keep your tires under-inflated.
Drive faster than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your tires with good tread depth.
questions.explanation: On wet roads, hydroplaning happens more often if tire pressure is too low or tire tread is worn. If you start to hydroplane, ease off the gas and push in the clutch to slow down.

questions.question: If you must drive in reverse, you should:

options.text: Drive as fast as possible to finish quickly.
Get out and walk the path to check for hazards first.
Use only the passenger side mirror.
Stick your head out the window to look back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out and walk the path to check for hazards first.
questions.explanation: Before backing up, walk around the vehicle to look for hazards. Use both mirrors while backing. Back up slowly at all times.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing in a placarded vehicle, you must:

options.text: Turn on your four-way flashers.
Stop within five feet of the tracks.
Change gears while on the tracks.
Change lanes while on the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your four-way flashers.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing, stop 15 to 50 feet from the tracks before crossing. Turn on your four-way flashers while crossing. Do not stop, change gears, or change lanes on the tracks.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you must be able to do all of the following about oil, except:

options.text: Show where the dipstick is located.
Show that the oil level is safe.
Show that the oil level is above the refill mark.
Show that the oil level is below the refill mark.

questions.correctAnswerText: Show that the oil level is below the refill mark.
questions.explanation: You must show where the oil dipstick is, confirm the oil level is safe, and show the oil level is above the refill mark. The oil level should never be below the refill mark.

questions.question: Service brakes should be tested:

options.text: Once a month.
Only by a trained mechanic.
Before every trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before every trip.
questions.explanation: Always test your brakes before driving. This helps you find problems before you need to stop on the road.

questions.question: If your engine catches fire, you should:

options.text: Open the hood right away.
Turn off the engine as soon as possible.
Not use a fire extinguisher.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the engine as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine immediately to stop the fire from spreading. Do not open the hood unless necessary.

questions.question: When starting from a stop, a vehicle should:

options.text: Shift to the right.
Be put into third gear.
Not roll backward.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not roll backward.
questions.explanation: Make sure your vehicle does not roll back when starting from a complete stop. This prevents hitting anything behind you.
